transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

It is not faulty and you do not need to send it back. The Eco 40-60 cycle is designed to take around 3–4 hours because it washes at lower temperatures for longer to save energy; this is normal behaviour, unlike your old machine which likely heated the water more aggressively. However, if you are worried about heating performance, please run a standard 60°C Cottons programme with a normal load. When that cycle finishes, check if the laundry is warm or still cold. This will tell us if the heater is working correctly.

I haven't run a 60°C Cottons wash, so I can't say how warm the laundry would be. On the Eco 40-60 the clothes come out clean, though the door glass is only barely lukewarm. Is that normal for an eco cycle?

Yes, that is completely normal. The Eco 40-60 cycle is designed to wash at lower temperatures for a longer duration to save energy and protect fabrics, so the water never gets hot enough to make the door glass warm. Since your clothes are coming out clean, the machine is working exactly as intended and you do not need to send it back.
